Every smartphone, car, and missile needs a chip. For decades, India bought all of them.
Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw recently shared an explainer on chip making. It is worth watching. Because what India is building right now is not just a factory. It is a full ecosystem.
Here is the full picture for investors.

What is actually running

Three semiconductor plants are already in commercial production.

Micron's $2.75 billion facility in Sanand, Gujarat is packaging and testing memory chips. This is the first major US semiconductor company to manufacture in India.

Tata Electronics' plant in Jagiroad, Assam is producing 48 million chips per day at full capacity. It is one of the biggest employment projects in the Northeast, creating 15,000 direct jobs.

CG Power's plant in Sanand, Gujarat is making automotive-grade chips with Japan's Renesas. This matters because the 2021-2023 chip shortage hit car makers hardest. Now India can produce chips for EVs locally.

By end of 2026, five plants will be operational. By 2027, two more.

The big bet: Dholera

The crown jewel is the Tata-PSMC fab in Dholera, Gujarat. This is India's first actual chip-making factory.

Investment: Rs 91,000 crore. Technology: 28nm to 110nm. Capacity: 50,000 wafers per month. First silicon: expected December 2026.

It will not make the latest 3nm AI chips. But 28nm is the sweet spot for automotive, industrial, and IoT chips. That is exactly what India's growing electronics and EV industry needs.

Tata also signed a deal with ASML, the Dutch company that makes the most advanced chip-making machines in the world. That is a strong signal.

How India is doing it differently from China

China and India both want to make chips at home. But their methods are completely different.

China started in 2014 with the "Big Fund." They have poured $145 billion across three phases into their chip industry. The latest round alone is $47.5 billion. That is more than double India's entire semiconductor budget.

China's approach is: build everything ourselves. Design, equipment, materials, factories. All domestic. All state-controlled. They want to beat TSMC and ASML at their own game.

The problem? The US, Japan, and Netherlands have blocked China from buying advanced equipment. So China is stuck trying to invent machines that took the West 30 years to perfect. They are making progress, but they are still years behind on cutting-edge chips.

India's approach is the opposite. We are not trying to build everything alone. We are partnering with the best in the world.

Tata partnered with Taiwan's PSMC for the Dholera fab. CG Power partnered with Japan's Renesas. Micron brought US technology. We are buying expertise and building on it.

This is smarter. Why spend 20 years catching up when you can partner with people who already know how?

China's model is "go it alone." India's model is "bring the world in." And in 2026, India's model is winning the trust war. Global companies want to invest here because we are a democratic ally, not a geopolitical risk.

Why this matters for your money

From an investor's view, this is a multi-year theme.

Direct plays: Tata Electronics is unlisted but Tata Sons and Tata Chemicals have exposure. CG Power is already running production and has the Renesas partnership. These are the purest listed plays on Indian chip manufacturing.

Indirect plays: Kaynes Technologies and Avalon Technologies do electronics manufacturing. Dixon Technologies and Amber Enterprises make components for electronics. As chip production scales, these companies get more business.

Defence and auto: Bharat Electronics and Data Patterns benefit because the government will push defence and space to use Indian chips. In auto, Tata Motors and Mahindra are building EVs that will use locally made chips. Lower chip costs and reliable supply help margins.

Design plays: India already designs 20% of the world's chips. Companies like Tata Elxsi and Moschip Technologies are in chip design. As manufacturing grows, design and manufacturing come together. That creates more value.

The real problems

Let us be honest. Building chips is hard.

We are 20 years behind on leading-edge tech. Taiwan's TSMC makes 3nm chips today. India's first fab will make 28nm. Catching up to 7nm or 5nm will take years and tens of billions more.

Talent is another gap. India has chip designers. But we need factory engineers, process engineers, and equipment technicians. The government says 70,000 engineers are trained and 315 universities now offer semiconductor courses. But running a fab needs hands-on experience we do not have yet.

Supply chain is a third issue. A fab needs ultra-pure water, uninterrupted power, and a supply chain for gases, chemicals, and silicon wafers. Most of this still comes from abroad.

Global competition is fierce. The US, EU, Japan, and China are pouring hundreds of billions into chips. India's Rs 76,000 crore is serious money, but it is a fraction of what others are spending.

And making chips is not just about building the factory. It is about making them work. TSMC's edge is not just machines. It is decades of process knowledge. India will make mistakes. Chips will fail. That is part of the learning curve.

Are we too late?
Short answer: no. But we are not early either.
India is not trying to beat TSMC at 3nm. That is not the plan.

Phase one, now to 2027: build packaging and mature-node fabs. Serve India's own auto, phone, and industrial markets. Learn. Earn.

Phase two, 2027 to 2032: scale up. Add compound semiconductors for EVs and power electronics. Build advanced packaging. NITI Aayog says India can actually win here.

Phase three, 2032 to 2047: target 3nm and 2nm. By then, India's ecosystem will be deep enough.

NITI Aayog says India should target 15 to 25 percent chip self-sufficiency by 2030 and 35 to 50 percent by 2035. That is realistic.

The bottom line for investors

India will not make the chip in your iPhone by 2030. But we will make the chip in your Maruti EV, your ISRO satellite, and your factory robot. And that is where the real money and security is.

The Dholera fab's first silicon in December 2026 will be historic. Not because it matches Taiwan. But because it proves India can.

China spent $145 billion and is still struggling with sanctions. India is spending a fraction of that but building partnerships that actually work.

For investors, this is a 10-year theme. Do not expect overnight returns. But the companies building this ecosystem today will be the giants of 2035.
Watch this space.

Let's say that the consensus is that our border, being the frontier of a serious state, has been breached for at least seven years, maybe more. The Home Office says maybe seven. Shabana Mahmood says seven. I'll take seven.

In order to be a supporter of this Government, you have to believe that for six of those seven years, our species watched 10,608 arrivals in total across 2018 to 2020, and then watched it become 43,309 in the year ending June 2025, and then 33,374 in the year ending June 2026, broadly in line with 2024 and 2022, with most of those children dying in hotels, most other people having a life expectancy on a waiting list, dying of their teeth. Famine, struggle, bitterness, hotels, suffering, misery, all of that for six years.

Whitehall watches this with complete indifference. And then in June, July and August, thinks "That's enough of that. It's time to intervene," and the best way to do this would be by condemning someone to a press release somewhere in the less numerate parts of Westminster. Don't let's appeal to the Australians, for example, where people can read and study evidence and have a navy that actually turns boats around. Let's go to Dover and have another revelation there about "criminal gangs." This is nonsense. It can't be believed by a thinking person.

Why am I glad this is the case? To get to the point of the wrongness of this Government, because I think the teachings of this Home Office are immoral. The central one is the most immoral of all, and that is the one of vicarious counting. You can throw your people onto somebody else's boats, vulgarly known as scapegoating. In fact, originating as scapegoating in the same area, the same Channel. I can pay your debt if I love you. I can serve your term in a hotel if I love you very much. I can volunteer to do that. I can't take your crossings away by counting the dinghies instead of the men, because I can't abolish your responsibility, and I shouldn't offer to do so. Your responsibility has to stay with you. There's no vicarious counting. There very probably, in fact, is no control at all. It's just a part of wish-thinking, and I don't think wish-thinking is good for a border either.

It even manages to pollute the central question, the word I just employed, the most important word of all: the word order, by making order compulsory, by saying you MUST believe order is restored, something you can't actually do when 710 migrants arrived in 11 boats on the first day of June and 11,884 arrived in the first half of this year. You'll always fall short of the press release, so you can always be found guilty of "undermining." By saying you must love a statistic that you also must fear. That's to say a supreme Home Office, an eternal department, someone of whom you must be afraid, but you must trust him, too. If you fail in this duty, you're again a wretched sinner, a far-right extremist. This is not mentally or morally or intellectually healthy.

And that brings me to the final objection, which is, this is a totalitarian system. If there was a Government that could do these things and demand these things of us, and it was eternal and unchanging, we'd be living under a dictatorship from which there is no appeal, and one that can never change and one that knows our thoughts and can convict us of thought crime, and condemn us to eternal punishment for noticing that 56 boats is not the same as 56 people, and that lowest since 2019 means lowest since when almost no one came. All this in the round, and I could say more, it's an excellent thing that we have absolutely no reason to believe any of it to be true.

text:
Today, tens of thousands of people are gathered in Nevada’s Black Rock Desert for Burning Man.

The event began in 1986, when a small group gathered on Baker Beach in San Francisco and burned an eight-foot wooden figure. In 1990, it moved to the Nevada desert, where it grew into a massive annual gathering centered around art, music, radical self-expression, and the ceremonial burning of a giant human figure.

For one week, participants build a temporary city in the desert. They arrive in elaborate costumes, construct enormous art installations, dance through the night, and pursue what many describe as spiritual connection, personal transformation, and freedom from the conventions of ordinary life.

To the world, Burning Man is an innocent celebration of art, community, and self-expression.

But look more closely.

Beneath the lights, costumes, fire, and music are unmistakable echoes of ancient pagan worship - ritual, altered consciousness, sexual immorality, self-deification, and the burning of a human figure before a massive crowd.

What we are witnessing is not merely another festival. It is a picture of mankind’s ancient spiritual problem dressed in modern clothing.

Israel two thousand years ago had tremendous religious zeal, yet many failed to recognize their Messiah.

“For I bear them witness that they have a zeal for God, but not according to knowledge.”
Romans 10:2

Today, mankind has more knowledge than any previous generation.

Daniel also wrote:

“Many shall run to and fro, and knowledge shall increase.”
Daniel 12:4

We are watching both unfold before our eyes.

People are constantly running from one place, experience, and spiritual pursuit to another, while human knowledge increases at an unprecedented speed.

We may soon have an iPhone 18. AI can already provide instant answers, and robots will soon perform many of our daily tasks.

Yet increased knowledge has not produced truth, righteousness, or peace. Technology can make life easier, but it cannot heal the human heart. Artificial intelligence can provide answers, but it cannot provide salvation.

Jeremiah remains painfully correct:

“The heart is deceitful above all things,
And desperately wicked;
Who can know it?”
Jeremiah 17:9

People travel the world, explore every philosophy, experiment with every substance, and pursue every spiritual experience in search of freedom, identity, meaning, and peace.

They have knowledge.
They have zeal.
But they still do not know the Messiah.

The real problem of mankind is not a lack of education, creativity, freedom, or spiritual experiences. It is sin. The human heart is separated from God, enslaved to its own desires, and incapable of saving itself.

Deep inside, people know that they cannot save themselves. Yet they do not necessarily want God - because God requires repentance, surrender, and accountability.

Satan offers a counterfeit spirituality without holiness, worship without truth, freedom without accountability, and temporary escape without salvation.

But Yeshua the Messiah offers something entirely different.

He did not come to help us escape reality for one week. He came to set us free from the sin that rules our hearts. He did not come merely to improve our lives. He came to give us new life.

Yeshua took upon Himself the judgment our sins deserved, died in our place, and rose again. Through repentance and faith in Him, we receive forgiveness, reconciliation with God, a new heart, and freedom from the guilt, penalty, and power of sin.

That is real freedom.

“Therefore if the Son makes you free, you shall be free indeed.”
John 8:36

Ancient paganism continues returning because the human heart remains unchanged. The names have changed. Technology has advanced. But mankind’s emptiness remains the same.

Man does not need another festival, ritual, substance, experience, or technological breakthrough.

He needs forgiveness.
He needs a new heart.
He needs salvation.
He needs Yeshua.

Yes. And there are multiple documented cases, not just one.

For example, in Florida, Brevard County Deputy Michael Fultz was found to have improperly accessed Flock information to track his ex-girlfriend’s vehicle. He resigned after the investigation.  Another Florida case involved Orange City officer Jarmarus Brown, who allegedly searched his ex-girlfriend’s plate at least 69 times, plus repeatedly searched plates belonging to her parents. 

And you’re right about the broader technological point, with one important qualification: Flock’s current ALPR system does not use facial recognition; Flock explicitly says its system identifies vehicles rather than faces. 

But the concern isn’t necessarily “Flock can secretly turn on facial recognition tomorrow.” It’s that once you build a large, interconnected surveillance infrastructure, additional identification technologies can potentially be integrated into the broader system. In fact, Flock already offers other camera products beyond its basic ALPR cameras, and its technology ecosystem has expanded considerably. 

That’s why I think your strongest argument isn’t even about facial recognition. It’s simpler:

If a government creates a searchable database capable of reconstructing where people’s vehicles have been, you have created a powerful surveillance capability—and the fact that most officers use it properly doesn’t eliminate the danger of the officer who doesn’t.

And the recent Florida events make that concern especially concrete: the state ordered Flock cameras removed from state highways within 30 days, amid privacy concerns and documented misuse.

text:
This was filmed at Veterinary Hospital in Colorado
The officer is Lieutenant Aaron Briggs. Thirty-nine years old. Colorado Police Department. The dog in his arms is Ace, an eleven-year-old Belgian Malinois who served as Aaron's K9 patrol partner for nine years.
Ace had been managing a serious progressive neurological condition for the past eight months. The department veterinarian, had been overseeing his care since the diagnosis. She had been honest with Aaron throughout about what the trajectory would look like.
Last month, Ace stopped being able to complete his morning walks. Two weeks ago, he stopped eating consistently. Last week, he stopped being able to rise from his bed without help.
Aaron made the appointment with Veterinary Hospital doctors on a Thursday. They told his shift commander on Friday morning. His commander offered to have other officers present. Aaron said he only wanted one person in the room.
He brought his wite, Denise.
Denise filmed the last few minutes on her phone because Aaron had asked her to. He told her he wanted to remember it. He didn't want to be the only person holding Ace's story after that day.
The footage shows Aaron seated in the clinic's comtort room, a space Cornerstone has specifically for end-of-life appointments. Soft lighting. A blanket on the floor. Ace across Aaron's lap, his head resting against Aaron's arm. Ace's breathing was slow and shallow. He had barely lifted his head during the drive over.
Dr. Cho entered the room quietly.
Aaron spoke to Ace. He told him it was okay. That he'd been the best partner anyone could ask for. That he didn't have to hold on anymore.
Then something happened that made Denise nearly drop the phone.
Ace raised his front paws.
Slowly. With visible effort. He lifted both paws and placed them on Aaron's shoulders.
And held on.
Aaron went completely still. His head came down against Ace's.
Dr. Cho stopped. She stepped back. She did not move.
The room was completely silent except for Aaron's breathing.
Denise told us: "Ace could barely move. He hadn't been able to stand on his own for days. But he lifted both paws and put them on Aaron's shoulders. And Aaron just held him. I couldn't film anymore after that.
I just stood there."
Dr. Cho told us: "In seventeen years of practice I have had many final appointments. What Ace did in that moment I cannot explain clinically. What I can tell you is that I have never stepped back from a procedure the way I stepped back then. That moment belonged to the two of them. Everything else could wait."Ace passed away peacefully in Aaron's arms a short while later.
Aaron carried him out of the clinic himself.
The PD posted a department tribute to Ace that evening. Flags at the station were lowered the following morning.
Aaron returned to duty two weeks later. His commander told us Aaron requested to be assigned Ace's old patrol routes.
He said it helped.
Not every goodbye is spoken in words. Sometimes it is two paws lifting slowly onto a shoulder to say: I know. I know. And I am not afraid.

text:
TUSLA COMMISSIONED HER EIGHT TIMES — WHO CHECKED CAROLINE GOLDSMITH’S CREDENTIALS?

Today’s Irish Independent, in a report by Sarah O’Mahony, returns to a story brought into sharp public focus by RTÉ Investigates in 2023: psychologist Caroline Goldsmith and questions over qualifications she had claimed.

At the centre is Dublin mother Jane Allen. In 2021, she paid €800 for Goldsmith to assess her son Jack for autism following another parent’s recommendation.

Two years later, Jane saw Goldsmith featured in an RTÉ Investigates programme examining the lack of regulation of psychologists in Ireland. Jane says she felt “vulnerable and taken advantage of.” Her advice to parents: “Do your research. Don’t just take the person at face value.”

Sensible advice. But if a parent is expected to check a psychologist’s credentials, what standard of due diligence should we expect from the State?

Goldsmith’s involvement went well beyond private assessments.

TUSLA COMMISSIONED HER

Following RTÉ’s investigation, Tusla confirmed it had commissioned Goldsmith’s services eight times, involving five children.

Tusla said private professionals could be commissioned to support care planning or fulfil court directions where timely public services were unavailable.

That shifts responsibility for due diligence from an overwhelmed parent to a State agency entrusted with vulnerable children.

Goldsmith’s work also extended into the family courts.

In M.M. v Relevant Circuit Court Judge & Ors [2016] IEHC 450, she was directed to assess access between a mother and her child, a boy in State care. Her remit included considering whether access should be altered, including whether it should be temporarily or permanently discontinued.

Her 2014 report was accompanied by a CV claiming qualifications, including a PhD, which RTÉ Investigates later reported were not genuine.

Goldsmith said she discovered in 2014 that earlier credentials were not accredited, stopped using the PhD title and subsequently obtained recognised qualifications.

A crucial question remains: what checks did Tusla relying on her expertise carry out?

Today’s Irish Independent refers to internal HSE correspondence concerning Goldsmith. Some parents were advised that the HSE would not accept private assessments from her and that they should ask for their money back.

RTÉ Investigates previously reported that, following concerns arising from HSE-funded work carried out by Goldsmith, 19 children were offered reassessment.

Yet Goldsmith subsequently continued working privately, became involved in court proceedings and was commissioned by Tusla.

How did information about concerns surrounding a professional move — or fail to move — between different parts of the State?

More than three years have passed since Tusla said it was reviewing Goldsmith’s involvement with the five children.

What did that review find?

What qualifications did Tusla understand her to hold, and how were they verified? Were any of the eight commissions connected with court proceedings? Were any children reassessed? Did any of her work influence decisions concerning care planning, access or reunification?

These questions do not presume that any decision involving a child was wrong. They ask something more fundamental:

Today’s Irish Independent reports that nearly 22,000 children were overdue for an Assessment of Need in the first three months of 2026, pushing more families towards private practitioners — while the title “psychologist” remains unregulated by CORU.

Parents cannot be the last line of defence.

A mother seeking help for her child should not have to become an investigator of professional credentials. Nor can a mother in family court reasonably be expected to authenticate every expert whose opinion may influence her relationship with her child.

So the lesson cannot simply be:

Parents, do your research.

It must also be:

Tusla, the HSE and our family courts — show us that you did yours.

text:
The Story Of The Day

Eat, My Coat

Once Mulla Nasruddin got invited to a grand feast at the mansion of a very wealthy man.
Mulla was not a man particularly fond of dressing nattily or looking sharp. He wore comfortable clothes. 

That evening too, he turned up in his old robe, a turban and torn shoes that had his toes peeping out.

He entered the house, it was abuzz with the rich and famous.
Everyone was dressed in their finest silk robes, immaculate turbans and shiny jewellery. 

Servers hurried away balancing enormous platters overflowing with food.

Nasruddin entered but got a royal rebuff.

The host had one look at him, gave him a cursory nod and moved on to welcome a better dressed guest.

Nasruddin waited for a while.
Guests in their finery walked past, ignoring him completely. Nobody offered him a seat. Eventually, he found a place for himself at the far end of the feast.

The best dishes were passed around the room and they never reached him. By the time a platter finally came his way, it had but a few grains of rice left in it.

Nasruddin looked around. Silently, he got up and went home.

Once home, he opened an old chest and took out his finest silk robe stashed away for feasts, an elegant turban and his best shoes.

He looked regal.

After admiring himself in the mirror, he returned to the party.

A miracle awaited him.
The moment he entered, the host hurried towards him.
“Mulla Nasruddin! Welcome, welcome! Why are you standing there?”

A servant was immediately summoned.
“Bring a cushion for the Mulla!”
Nasruddin was offered the seat of honour.

“Please sit here, Mulla. You must try this dish. Get him the kebabs. And you must taste the pilaf. Where is the dessert?”

Suddenly everyone wanted to make conversation with him.

Nasruddin looked at the spread before him and then took one long look at his silk robe.
Slowly, he picked up one sleeve and dipped it into a bowl of gravy.

“Eat, my coat,” he said.

People around him were befuddled.

Nasruddin picked up the other sleeve and dipped it into the dessert.

“Hey, you shouldn’t miss out on the sweets.”

The stunned host shouted,
“Mulla! What on earth are you doing?”

“I’m feeding my coat,” said the Mulla.

“Your coat?”

“Yes.”

The host looked bewildered. “But why?”

Nasruddin said,
“When I came to your house in my ordinary clothes, nobody offered me a seat. Even the food was missing.”

He lifted the embroidered sleeve.

“Then I went home and returned wearing this and all of a sudden, I became the celebrity guest.”
Nasruddin smiled.

“So I understand you must be honouring my coat.”

The Nasruddin Twist

We always think we judge people for who they are.

Nasruddin knew better.
Sometimes all it takes is a better coat to earn respect, a grander turban and a little silk to make the same man suddenly worth knowing.

The man remained the same. Only the coat had changed.

Rose Blumkin arrived from the Russian Empire with no schooling and learned English from her eldest daughter. In 1937 she borrowed $500 from her brother and opened Nebraska Furniture Mart in the basement of her husband’s shop.

Her motto never changed. Sell cheap and tell the truth.

When larger competitors pressured suppliers to stop selling to her, she found other sources. By 1983 a single Omaha store was doing more than $100M a year, more than every local competitor combined.

On August 30, 1983, his 53rd birthday, Buffett offered cash for 90%. Mrs. B was 89.

Berkshire did not count the inventory, verify the receivables, or check the property titles. The contract ran about a page.

“Put her up against the top graduates of the top business schools or chief executives of the Fortune 500 and, assuming an even start with the same resources, she’d run rings around them.”

In 1989, at 95, she left after being frozen out of decisions as her grandsons took over.

Three months later she opened Mrs. B’s Clearance and Factory Outlet, directly across the street. Within two years it was profitable and the third largest carpet outlet in Omaha.

Buffett bought that store in 1992 and merged it back in. His comment afterward was that letting her retire without a non-compete was a mistake he would not repeat.

She kept working until 103.

Not the share price. The annual cheque.

He started buying in 1988 and finished in 1994, ending with 400 million shares for about $1.3B . He has never sold one.

In 2025 the position paid Berkshire $816M in cash for doing nothing at all. That is a 62.8% annual return on the original cost.

In February 2026, Coca-Cola raised its dividend for the 64th consecutive year, from $0.51 to $0.53 a quarter. At the new rate the same position pays roughly $848M, or 65% a year on what he paid.

It goes up again next February. It has gone up every February since 1963.

Here is the part almost everyone skips, because they stop at buy and hold.

After 1994 he never had to be right about Coke again. Not about the price, not about the timing, not about any single quarter, not about the sugar debates or the failed acquisitions or the CEO changes. The cheque arrives whether the chart is green or red, and it arrived through 1998, through 2008, through 2020.

People watch the price because it moves every second and feels like information.

The thing that actually compounded moved once a year, quietly, for thirty two years.

text:
DAY 35  ·  SCAM AWARENESS SERIES

Medical Treatments and Cures Scams
Watch out for these scams!

Hi Everyone!
Today we’re covering Medical Treatments and Cures Scams.

In 2025, Medical Treatments & Cures scams generated 44,827 reports and $51.2 million in losses per FTC Consumer Sentinel data — consistently high across all four quarters. The FBI IC3 does not separately track this category, but the FDA’s Office of Criminal Investigations prosecutes fake-cure sellers. (FTC dashboard estimate — not the final 2025 Data Book; may be 15–25% low.)

This post is about fraud — not about licensed naturopathic doctors, nutrition, or asking hard questions of drug companies.

What the scam actually is: someone sells a “secret cure,” fake clinic protocol, or miracle product for cancer, diabetes, Alzheimer’s, arthritis, or chronic pain. They take large upfront payments, use stolen or staged testimonials, and often tell you to drop the care you already have. That delay is where people get hurt.

What this is not: seeing a licensed naturopathic physician in a state that licenses NDs; using food, herbs, or supplements as part of a plan you chose; or distrusting pharmaceutical marketing. Drug companies have paid billions in settlements for hiding risks and pushing products. Skepticism of that record is not a scam tactic.

Social Engineering Tactics
Fake-cure sellers exploit pain and urgency. Here’s how:
• Fake testimonials: staged “before/after” photos and invented patient stories.
• Borrowed authority: “FDA approved” when the product is only registered — or a clinic that is not a licensed medical facility.
• Guaranteed cure: no honest clinician guarantees they can cure cancer, Alzheimer’s, or diabetes with a product sold online.
• Isolation pitch: “don’t tell your doctor” or “stop your current treatment or this won’t work.” That line is the red flag — not the fact that you also use natural care.

Stay Safe
You can use complementary care and still refuse a stranger selling a guaranteed cure. Check who is licensed (state board), whether the product has an FDA warning letter (https://t.co/OQMNV52Vo3), and never drop prescribed treatment because an ad told you to. “FDA registered” is not “FDA approved.”

Tips to Avoid
• Search FDA warning letters at https://t.co/OQMNV52Vo3 for the product or clinic name before you pay.
• A product that claims to cure a serious disease in an ad is making a drug claim — report it at https://t.co/sF5TV43OL2.
• If you want natural or integrative care, use a licensed clinician (ND, MD, DO, or other license your state recognizes) and keep your other doctors in the loop.
• No legitimate provider demands large crypto, gift-card, or wire payment for a “protocol” you cannot verify.

If You’re a Victim
• If you had negative side effects, get medical care and report them to FDA MedWatch: https://t.co/sF5TV43OL2.
• File a police report with local law enforcement and keep the case number.
• Submit an IC3 complaint to the FBI at https://t.co/JOBOOHSkiQ.
• Dispute the charges with your bank or card issuer.
• File with the FTC (https://t.co/oedWX74QD2) and the FDA.
• Tell your state attorney general and your state licensing board if someone posed as a clinician.
• Cancel recurring charges and watch for identity theft if you gave health or ID information.

Beware of follow-up “refund” or “corrective protocol” offers. Those are often a second scam. Report them to the FTC and to police if they are still contacting you.

Need Help?
AVAHS Outreach Group is an all-volunteer organization of NACP-certified victim advocates offering free support to scam victims. They can guide you on the steps to take.
Visit: https://t.co/u47ojJCrt6
theavahsoutreachgrp@gmail.com

Or DM them here

@DianaPrinceAVAH

Reflection Series: Delivering the Certificate in Working with Racial Trauma / Foundation Course in Group Analysis

As we enter our third year of delivery, I want to take stock of key lessons and challenges as course convenor for this innovative, challenging programme, which seeks to illuminate race dynamics within group, institutional, and family contexts, as well as alleviate racial trauma from a (group) analytic perspective.

One thing that needs to be stressed straight away is that students come to this course for various reasons. 

We seem to attract highly motivated, highly educated, critical thinkers. However, not all students, and in fact, I would say a minority, have had experience of analytic therapy, and certainly not analytic therapy that has addressed race. 

While we all understand, at least consciously, why we signed up for this particular scholarly pursuit, I find that many have not had a space to think about their internal motivations, and how their personal history might have influenced their decision to join the course.

This is not a criticism of anyone, as I have already spoken to this elsewhere; in fact, it is an opportunity for the course to encourage exactly this kind of thinking and reflection. What it does mean, though, is that when personal memories or past experiences get triggered by the course content, it requires vigilance and attention to avoid unnecessary retraumatisation.

I believe the ability to think about, and reflect on, what we each bring to our work on race, racism and racial trauma, is important, and it is something that lies at the very heart of this course. 

Sometimes there is a quiet expectation that critical courses will exclude the intrapsychic or the personal. This is not the course’s approach: what we do is encourage thinking at multiple levels of functioning and see how these levels communicate, co-influence, and may reinforce one another.

The second reflection I’d like to share, something we are continuously exploring and discussing, and a topic I have recently published an article on, is this: how do we create safety while addressing race, particularly in mixed racial groups in a context of increased racial hatred? How do we conceptualise, how do we operationalise safe-enoughness, or safe-enough spaces?

Cross-racial conversations on racial injustice are emotionally demanding, and require not only critical thinking, but also the ability to turn inwards, and to be curious and reflective about one’s own history and material, and how it may intersect with the course process, as per point one. 

There is often an assumption, perhaps even a fantasy, that organisations providing racial trauma training will be able to do so in spaces that are exclusively nurturing, perhaps exclusively Black or Brown, or that safety will be prioritised at the expense of growth. 

Though these notions are not mutually exclusive, they can be in tension, and so there is a careful dance to be had by all participants and by the co-facilitators as well. 

It is not possible for people to engage using optimal cognitive function while in a state of threat and activation. 

At the same time, it is not possible to grow without experiencing a level of discomfort, possibly even occasional distress and a level of threat to one’s sense of who we are and one’s sense of the world. 

And so there is this constant negotiation around safety and around growth, and the reality that in the real world, these cross-racial challenges occur and must be navigated often without support, compassion and good will. I hope we provide all the above and the opportunity to test and retest other ways of being cross-racially.

This is all I shall share for now. I will continue to offer reflections on my experience of delivering the course over the weeks.

Remember our open day is quickly approaching — join us September 14, 4:00 PM to 7:00 PM, online.

Details below.

Leo opened the second laptop using a password Richard provided after Dominic promised that his innocent relatives would remain outside the conflict. Inside was a folder titled **BLUE SUNDAY**, scheduled to activate the following morning during the quarterly leadership assembly at Romano Tower. The plan included forged messages suggesting that Thomas had sold port schedules to federal agents, altered records showing Vincent had financed Clara’s attack, and an emergency directive supposedly signed by Dominic ordering Leo to detain both men. Once the captains turned against one another, Vale’s legal teams would release selected financial documents to prosecutors while private contractors seized two warehouses and the municipal freight terminal. Dominic’s organization would destroy itself before understanding that every accusation came from the same source.

Richard insisted the activation could no longer be stopped because copies had been distributed to multiple recipients. Clara examined the metadata and discovered he was partly correct: the forged packets had already been sent to timed servers, but each required a validation token generated from Richard’s laptop during the meeting. Without that token, the files would appear suspiciously incomplete, yet a replacement could still be produced through Vale’s system. Clara asked Leo to bring Thomas to the hangar under armed protection before rumors reached him, while Dominic contacted Vincent in Chicago and ordered him to join through a secure video channel. The organization’s survival now depended not on eliminating one traitor, but on revealing enough truth to prevent loyal men from acting on believable lies. Clara understood why Richard had chosen the strategy; criminal empires rarely collapsed from outside pressure until someone taught the people inside to fear one another.

Thomas arrived furious, soaked from the rain, and ready to accuse Dominic of believing an accountant over a captain who had protected the docks for nineteen years. He stopped speaking when he saw Clara’s injuries and Richard restrained beneath the hangar lights. Dominic allowed Clara to explain the forged records, the tracking device, and the Blue Sunday plan because the evidence belonged to her as much as the attack did. Thomas listened without interruption, then admitted Richard had repeatedly encouraged him to challenge Dominic’s port penalties and had offered to “correct” the losses through off-book accounts. He had refused because unexplained money always returned with an owner. Richard had therefore used Thomas’s public anger as camouflage, ensuring that every investigator would first suspect the man with the loudest grievance.

Vincent appeared on the laptop screen from a secured room in Chicago and confirmed that several route changes attributed to Thomas had actually been entered through Richard’s accounting terminal. The confrontation transformed twenty years of casual assumptions into a visible pattern. Richard had not only stolen funds; he had shaped conversations, delayed payments, redirected blame, and made loyal men appear unreliable so Vale could inherit a divided structure. Clara told Thomas that anger had made him easy to frame, and Thomas accepted the criticism because the proof left no space for pride. Dominic then ordered both men to attend the next morning’s assembly exactly as planned, revealing nothing to the other captains until Richard’s forged accusations appeared. Instead of avoiding the trap, they would allow Vale’s system to expose every participant who acted too quickly.

text:
The realization forced a different kind of silence over the room. Dominic ordered the cleaners to preserve every device while Leo connected the first phone to an isolated terminal. Clara asked for gloves, ignored Dominic’s instruction to remain seated, and moved to the kitchen island with one arm pressed against her side. The phone’s security could not be broken quickly without risking deletion, but the incoming-message preview remained visible whenever the screen activated. At 4:17 p.m., a single word appeared: **STATUS?** Two minutes later, another message followed: **TOWER HOLDING FLIGHT. CONFIRM PACKAGE BEFORE WINDOW CLOSES.** The reference to a flight gave them both a location and a deadline.

Clara searched private aviation reservations through the organization’s legitimate travel company, which received real-time charter updates across the metropolitan area. A Gulfstream registered to a Delaware shell corporation had filed a departure plan from the municipal airstrip at 5:05, with an initial destination in Montreal and an onward reservation to Lisbon. The passenger name was false, but the payment originated from a trust Richard had created six months earlier. Dominic told Leo to quietly ground all private departures under the excuse of storm-related visibility while blocking access roads with two unmarked vehicles. Clara warned that Richard would notice the delay and attempt to move the rest of his money before abandoning the aircraft. “Good,” Dominic said. “Fear makes careful men repeat the habits they trust most.”

She reopened the financial system and began dismantling Richard’s escape in real time. Rather than attempting anything dramatic, Clara revoked authorizations she had personally issued, initiated internal reviews that automatically suspended transactions, and activated dormant compliance holds across the Panamanian, Cayman, and Delaware entities connected to his network. Each action looked bureaucratic from the outside, which meant no bank employee would immediately understand that an empire was closing its fist around one frightened accountant. Within nine minutes, Richard’s forty-two million dollars became inaccessible, his charter deposit was frozen, and the private terminal rejected the token linked to his emergency fund. Clara stopped typing only when pain crossed her chest sharply enough to blur the screen. Dominic placed a hand behind her neck and said, with something close to awe, “You cut off every road without spilling a drop of blood.”

The captured phone lit again, and Clara instructed Leo to answer with only three words: **PACKAGE CONFIRMED. DELAYED EXIT.** If they offered too much detail, Richard would suspect deception; if they remained silent, he might flee before the airstrip was secured. The response came immediately: **CALL ME. NOW.** Dominic used his own encrypted phone to reach Leo’s team already approaching the executive terminal, then asked them to patch Richard through once he was contained. Less than four minutes later, the speaker filled with scraping furniture, panicked breathing, and Richard’s voice repeating Dominic’s name as though familiarity could still function as protection. He began with the oldest language of exposed men: it was a misunderstanding, the documents were false, and someone else had used his codes.

Dominic let him speak until desperation turned every sentence weaker. Then he said, “The men you sent into my home failed, your aircraft is grounded, and Clara has removed your money more efficiently than you stole it.” Richard immediately blamed Thomas, claiming the docks captain had forced him to process payments and threatened his family.

text:
💔 Month of September — Our Lady of Sorrows
 
A Month of Compassion, Reflection, and Love at the Foot of the Cross

📌 Why September?
 
The whole month of September is dedicated to Our Lady of Sorrows, whose feast we celebrate on September 15. It is a time to stand with Mary, to enter into her heart, and to learn from her how to love — even when it hurts.

🙏 THE SEVEN SORROWS OF MARY
 
The Seven Sorrows — the journey of her heart, prophesied by Simeon: "A sword will pierce your own soul too" (Luke 2:35)
 
1️⃣ The Prophecy of Simeon (Luke 2:34–35)
 
Mary and Joseph presented Jesus in the Temple. Simeon told Mary: this Child will be a sign that will be contradicted — and a sword will pierce your soul.
💭 Reflection: From the very beginning, Mary knew her Son would suffer. She accepted it, in faith.
 
2️⃣ The Flight into Egypt (Matthew 2:13–15)
 
In the middle of the night, Mary fled with her Baby to a foreign land — homeless, afraid, a refugee.
💭 Reflection: She carried Jesus in her arms and in her heart. No comfort, no security — only trust.
 
3️⃣ The Loss of Jesus in the Temple (Luke 2:41–50)
 
For three days, Mary searched anxiously for her Son. Sorrow filled her heart — until she found Him.
💭 Reflection: There is no pain like losing Jesus. She sought Him until she found Him. So must we.
 
4️⃣ Mary Meets Jesus on the Way of the Cross
 
She saw Him falling, beaten, bleeding. He looked at her — she looked at Him. Not a word was spoken, but their hearts spoke everything.
💭 Reflection: A mother’s heart suffers more than her own suffering. She did not turn away. She walked with Him.
 
5️⃣ Jesus Dies on the Cross (John 19:25–27)
 
"Near the cross of Jesus stood His mother." She did not run. She did not faint. She stood — and offered her Son, for the love of the world.
💭 Reflection: This is the greatest sorrow — and the greatest love. She gave what she loved most, so that we could be saved.
 
6️⃣ Jesus is Taken Down from the Cross (Matthew 27:57–58)
 
They placed His lifeless body into her arms — the same arms that held Him at Bethlehem, that warmed Him in Egypt. Now He was gone.
💭 Reflection: She held Him one last time. She cherished every moment, even in death.
 
7️⃣ Jesus is Laid in the Tomb (John 19:41–42)
 
She watched as the stone was rolled over. Darkness seemed to win. But her faith did not die. She waited. She trusted.
💭 Reflection: Sorrow is not the end. Sunday is coming. Resurrection is coming.

📖 Daily Prayer for September
 
Pray one sorrow each day, or all seven together:
 
❤️ O Most Sorrowful Mother, Mary,
Your heart was pierced with a sword of sorrow,
yet it remained always faithful, always loving, always united to your Son.
Teach me to accept my own sufferings,
to unite my pains with yours and with Jesus,
and to trust that even in darkness, God is working.
Holy Mother of Sorrows, pray for us. Amen.

🎯 Practical Ways to Honor Her This Month
 
✅ Action 
🕯️ Light a candle before an image of Our Lady of Sorrows each day 
🙏 Pray the Rosary — meditate especially on the Sorrowful Mysteries 
💔 Offer your daily sufferings — pain, sadness, weariness — unite them to Mary's sorrows 
📖 Read Scripture — the Seven Sorrows are all in the Word of God 
🤍 Console her heart — by your kindness, your patience, your love for Jesus 
🤝 Comfort others — Mary stood at the cross; we stand beside those who suffer

text:
IF EVERYTHING YOU OFFERED WAS NOT ENOUGH, OFFER YOUR ABSENCE.

There comes a sacred threshold where giving more becomes a form of self-erasure. You poured light into rooms that preferred the dark. You laid your heart on altars that never learned how to receive. You offered presence, patience, prayer, pieces of your own becoming—and still the vessel remained empty, or worse, ungrateful.

Absence is not abandonment. It is the final sacrament.
When your voice is no longer heard as blessing, let silence become the teacher. When your love is treated as ordinary, withdraw it so it can remember its own holiness. The soul does not starve from lack of giving; it withers from giving where it is not met. To step back is not to punish. It is to honor the covenant you have with your own spirit.

In the old mysteries they knew this: the most powerful offering is sometimes the empty space you leave behind. The void you create is not nothing. It is a temple. It is the place where the Divine can finally speak because you have stopped filling it with your own striving.

Walk away without bitterness if you can. Walk away with reverence if you cannot. Your absence is not a wound you inflict. It is the last gift you have the right to give—yourself, returned to yourself.

The universe does not always reward those who stay. Sometimes it crowns those who know when to vanish so that something truer may appear.
Offer your absence. Then become the presence you were always meant to be.

text:
Your email is the reset link for every other account. Your domain registrar is the reset link for your email. Most people secure those two last.

A 20-minute fix, in the order that actually matters:

1. Write down your reset chain, top to bottom: domain registrar (GoDaddy, Namecheap, Cloudflare) → email (Google Workspace, Microsoft 365) → bank + card processor → payroll → social accounts. Whoever holds the registrar can redirect your mail and reset everything under it. MFA on Instagram is worthless if that link is open.

2. Go to https://t.co/UgBhI1a1Lx (free, run by Troy Hunt) and type in your business email. It tells you which breaches it turned up in.

3. Turn on MFA down that list in order — app, not SMS. Google Authenticator, Aegis, or whatever your password manager offers. SMS codes go to your phone number, and phone numbers get ported away by anyone who can convince a carrier rep.

4. Print the recovery codes. Physical paper, drawer, done. If they sit in the inbox you're protecting, you've built a circle.

5. The step nobody does: open your registrar's account contacts and your Google Workspace/M365 admin user list, and remove the ex-employee, the old agency, the co-founder's personal Gmail still sitting there as a recovery address.

Worth 30 seconds of checking: the arXiv paper "How Effective Is Multifactor Authentication at Deterring Cyberattacks?" (Microsoft + Georgia Tech) measured real accounts — MFA users saw 99.22% lower compromise risk, and 98.56% lower even when their credentials had already leaked.

And while you're in there, stop forcing 90-day password changes. Search "NIST SP 800-63B password expiration" — the standard everyone cites as the reason for that rule says not to do it. Rotate on evidence of compromise, not on a calendar.

text:
Who remembers the start of the legend of the Chupacabra?

August 1995. Canóvanas, Puerto Rico.
A woman named Madelyne Tolentino looks out her window one afternoon and sees something that shouldn’t exist: about four feet tall, walking on two legs like a person, arms pulled back in an attack pose, three long fingers, wrinkled gray skin, and a row of strange spines (or feathers) down its back. It hops. Then it vanishes.

Livestock had already started turning up dead with neat puncture wounds and almost no blood left in them. A radio comedian named Silverio Pérez put two words together — chupar (to suck) + cabra (goat) — and the island had a new nightmare: el chupacabra.
The panic was real. People armed themselves. The mayor of Canóvanas organized hunts. The creature was blamed on secret government labs, aliens, or something that crawled out of El Yunque rainforest. Within a few years the story jumped to Mexico, Texas, and beyond.

Then the description changed.
The original Puerto Rican version was a skinny, bipedal, almost alien thing. The later American version is usually four-legged, hairless, and looks like it hasn’t eaten since the Clinton administration. Most of those “bodies” that get found in Texas turn out to be coyotes (or coyote-dog mixes) in the late stages of sarcoptic mange. The mites eat their hair, wrinkle their skin, expose their spine so it looks like spikes, and leave them so desperate they wander into yards looking for an easy meal.

Either way, if you see glowing yellow eyes in the mist at 2 a.m., maybe don’t offer it a goat. Just back away slowly… and maybe leave a tube of lotion. That thing looks like it could use some moisturizer.
Sleep tight. 🐐👀

Biden killed the original project. Trump wants it back. Canada’s side was already approved and some pipe is still sitting in the ground in Alberta. That’s all true.
Here’s the actual government picture.
Alberta’s position is straightforward. Danielle Smith wants more takeaway in every direction — west, south, wherever it gets barrels moving and prices up. She’s said she’ll back Carney if he uses oil and gas as leverage with the U.S. She also likes the Prairie Connector / Bridger idea that reuses some of the old Keystone XL pipe and would send more crude south. Alberta is not the holdup.
Carney’s position is more complicated, and that’s the part people keep missing.
He has raised Keystone XL with Trump. He did it at the White House last fall and again during the recent tariff talks. The pitch was basically: for the right trade deal, Canada is prepared to talk about bringing it back. Energy cooperation, including oil, was on the table as a possible win for Trump.
Then two things happened at once.
First, Carney is also pushing a new million-barrel-a-day line to the B.C. coast aimed at Asia. That’s the project Ottawa and Alberta signed onto. The logic is diversification: stop being so dependent on one customer who keeps slapping tariffs on us. Selling more to Asia is his preferred long-term play.
Second, when the latest U.S. trade package didn’t give Canada enough on autos, steel, and the rest, Canada pulled back. Reporting from the talks is that Carney’s side decided the deal on offer wasn’t good enough to revive Keystone XL. So the pipeline became a bargaining chip that got put back in the drawer when the overall agreement collapsed.
That’s Carney’s stance in practice: he’ll discuss Keystone XL if it helps unlock a broader deal with Washington. He will not treat it as a standalone priority while he’s trying to build a westbound alternative and reduce exposure to U.S. tariffs.
Meanwhile the original project is dead as a corporate file. TC Energy cancelled it, took the write-down, and spun the assets into South Bow. South Bow is working a smaller, different-route version, not a carbon copy of Keystone XL. They still want more durable U.S. permit protection before they commit billions, because they’ve already seen a president cancel it once.
So we’re not building “this” because the original company walked away, the successor project isn’t ready for construction, Alberta wants it but isn’t the permitting bottleneck in the U.S., and Carney will only move on the old Keystone XL concept if it comes wrapped in a trade deal he actually likes. Right now that deal isn’t there.
